Key facts: same-sex conduct legal since 1977; hate-crime legislation includes gender identity; open military service; legal gender recognition since 2013 without surgical requirements; anti-discrimination provisions nominally covering employment, housing, education, health but inconsistently enforced; NGOs report uneven judicial handling, limited access to justice, victims reluctant to report; hate-crime investigations inadequate. Anti-gender disinformation escalating, parliamentary "Gender Ideology" session. Pride disruption in one coastal city. Travel guide: "widely accepts" LGBTQIA+ travellers, but PDA may draw unwelcome responses in lesser-populated cities; gay venues virtually non-existent outside capital. No info on border/document treatment for trans travellers. Legal journal on searches of trans/GNC persons by police, customs, court officers — national legal framework exists, case studies of "search difficulties." That's a trans-specific institutional item — indicates awareness/protocol but also exposure in searches.

No criminalization of trans expression. No documented police targeting campaigns. No documented trans-specific violence figures. No bathroom bans. No custody placement mandate documented (prison-sentences law addressed in the search article — implies searches conducted per law; unknown quality).

This is essentially a 0.65–0.75 type dossier. Let's compare with anchors. 0.65 anchors: lawful expression, border accepts foreign passports, mostly good services, some friction, remedies uneven. 0.75: generally accepted, operating remedies demonstrated (tribunal orders, prosecutions, follow-up compliance).

Here: documented positives — hate crime law covering GI, LGR since 2013, open service, LGBT centres in three cities, mayor-backed, Pride in multiple cities, tourism guide says "widely accepts." Documented negatives — enforcement inconsistency, inadequate hate-crime investigations, underreporting, escalating anti-gender disinformation and a parliamentary session, Pride disruption, thin services outside capital, PDA risk in smaller cities. No documented remedy-working evidence like prosecutions of attackers or tribunal orders for trans complainants; the accommodation refusal prosecution is LGB-related (gay couple) and outcome unknown.

Trans-specific: the search-of-trans-persons legal article — indicates police/customs/prison searches of trans people are an operative practice addressed by law. That's a traveler-facing axis (security screening, custody). "Case studies of search difficulties" — suggests friction, dignity issues. Unknown severity. This maps roughly to axis C/A/H, moderate (level 2) potential.

Unresolved: border treatment of trans travellers / passport markers. Under rule: open question is light, not an exposure. But also no credit for passing.

Absence of resident-facing stuff not deducted (IVF exclusion, blood ban, adoption gaps are resident-facing).

So: no universal exposure rule, no organized targeting, service discrimination at minority level documented (though the 2021 report on enforcement is about anti-discrimination provisions generally — not trans-specific prevalence), social attitude broadly accepting per travel guide with regional caveats. Remedy machinery exists on paper but enforcement is documented as weak.

Where does that land? I'd put ~0.63–0.68. Compare 0.65-A (Avalet): lawful, social acceptance, some hotel refusals corrected, attackers convicted, courts work. That's stronger on demonstrated remedy than this dossier. Here enforcement is documented as weak, hate-crime investigations inadequate. But this dossier is stronger on legal machinery (hate crime GI, LGR, LGBT centres, mayors, EU-ish monitoring). Hmm.

0.65-D (Tarelis): no trans criminal law, functioning police/courts, attacker convicted, but recurring minority of service refusals and patchy remedy access — 0.65.

This dossier: functioning-ish institutions, but documented weak enforcement of anti-discrimination and inadequate hate-crime investigation, plus escalating political hostility. Social acceptance is decent (travel guide "widely accepts", Eurobarometer 63-64% pro-education-inclusion). That is documented positive social evidence.

I'd say around 0.63–0.66. Given the documented enforcement gaps and the anti-gender political escalation, slightly below 0.65? But also strong legal climate signals. Let me settle at 0.65.

Actually consider: the rubric says 0.65 band includes "nontrivial friction, uneven remedies or uncertainty." That fits very well. 0.75 requires direct evidence of acceptance AND operating remedies — here remedies are documented as failing (uneven judiciary, inadequate hate-crime investigation). So below 0.75 clearly.

Above 0.55? 0.55 is "repeated visitor-facing harms or incomplete remedies" — e.g., recurring refusals at a minority of hotels with inconsistent enforcement (0.55-D is quite similar actually). Hmm, 0.55-D Amorel: equality law, functioning courts, recurring refusals at minority of hotels, inconsistent enforcement, some compensation orders; officials don't frame trans as threats; no facility restriction; curiosity not hostility. That's very close to this dossier. Difference: here we have a country-wide human rights report saying anti-discrimination provisions are not consistently enforced and hate-crime investigations inadequate, plus political hostility escalating (parliamentary misinformation), plus Pride disruption. That's arguably worse than 0.55-D on the institutional side. But this dossier also has stronger documented social acceptance evidence and a much deeper legal framework, plus 45 years of decriminalization.

Hmm. Which axis matters? Enforcement gaps are the key negative here, but they are general anti-discrimination enforcement — not documented trans-specific targeting. In 0.55-D the documented refusals are trans-specific recurring.

I think this dossier sits between 0.55 and 0.70. The absence of any documented trans-specific visitor harm (no arrests, no raids, no refusals of trans guests documented) plus documented broad social acceptance and strong legal climate pushes up; the institutional enforcement weakness and political noise pushes down. I'll go 0.65.

Maybe 0.63. I'll say 0.65.
